questions.title: SGB election voter turnout, comparative food prices and Mathematical Literacy terminology

subQuestions.questionText:
School X and School Y conducted an election for new members to serve on the school governing body (SGB). The double bar graph titled 'NUMBER OF VOTERS PER TIME SLOT AT SCHOOL X AND SCHOOL Y' shows the number of voters voting during different time slots at the two schools. The values read from the graph are:

| Time slot | School X | School Y |
|---|---|---|
| 15:00–15:30 | 0 (no bar) | 18 |
| 15:30–16:00 | 0 (no bar) | 12 |
| 16:00–16:30 | 10 | 5 |
| 16:30–17:00 | 12 | 9 |
| 17:00–17:30 | 26 | 26 |
| 17:30–18:00 | 30 | 24 |
| 18:00–18:30 | 18 | 5 |
| 18:30–19:00 | 8 | 2 |

Write down the number of voters at School Y from 16:00–16:30.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 & 2: **5** (five) (2A correct number)

Teaching point: Find the 16:00–16:30 group on the horizontal axis and read the height of the School Y (patterned) bar only — it stops at 5. The taller solid bar next to it (10) belongs to School X.

The double bar graph 'NUMBER OF VOTERS PER TIME SLOT AT SCHOOL X AND SCHOOL Y' gives the following number of voters:

| Time slot | School X | School Y |
|---|---|---|
| 15:00–15:30 | 0 (no bar) | 18 |
| 15:30–16:00 | 0 (no bar) | 12 |
| 16:00–16:30 | 10 | 5 |
| 16:30–17:00 | 12 | 9 |
| 17:00–17:30 | 26 | 26 |
| 17:30–18:00 | 30 | 24 |
| 18:00–18:30 | 18 | 5 |
| 18:30–19:00 | 8 | 2 |

Identify the time slot when 30 people voted at School X.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: **17:30** (1A for 17:30 / 5:30 pm / half past five)
Mark 2: **18:00** (1A for 18:00 / 6:00 pm / 6 o'clock)

So the time slot is **17:30 – 18:00**.

OR

5:30 pm – 6:00 pm (1A + 1A)

OR

Half past five until 6 o'clock in the afternoon/evening (1A + 1A)

Teaching point: Both ends of the time slot must be given to earn both marks — a single time such as "17:30" only earns one mark.

subQuestions.questionText:
The number of voters at School Y per time slot was:

| Time slot | School Y |
|---|---|
| 15:00–15:30 | 18 |
| 15:30–16:00 | 12 |
| 16:00–16:30 | 5 |
| 16:30–17:00 | 9 |
| 17:00–17:30 | 26 |
| 17:30–18:00 | 24 |
| 18:00–18:30 | 5 |
| 18:30–19:00 | 2 |

Choose the statement (A–C) below that BEST describes the trend of the voters at School Y.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: **C** — The number of voters decreased, then increased and finally decreased with time. (2A correct option)

Teaching point: Track the School Y values in order: 18 → 12 → 5 (a decrease), then 9 → 26 (an increase), then 24 → 5 → 2 (a decrease again). Option A is wrong because the numbers do not start by increasing, and option B is wrong because the numbers do not end by picking up again.

subQuestions.questionText:
During the 17:30–18:00 time slot 30 voters voted at School X and 24 voters voted at School Y. The probability of randomly selecting a voter from School X is 0,56 during the 17:30–18:00 time slot.

Write 0,56 as a simplified fraction.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $\dfrac{56}{100}$ (1A writing as a fraction)
Mark 2: $= \dfrac{14}{25}$ (1A simplification)

Teaching point: 0,56 means 56 hundredths, so write it as $\dfrac{56}{100}$ first. Then divide the numerator and the denominator by their highest common factor, 4: $56 \div 4 = 14$ and $100 \div 4 = 25$.

subQuestions.questionText:
The newly elected SGB planned to have lunch with the staff. TABLE 1 below shows the average comparative food prices for May 2022 and May 2023 needed for some of the lunch items.

**TABLE 1: COMPARATIVE FOOD PRICES FOR SOME LUNCH ITEMS**

| Food items | Price May 2022 (R) | Price May 2023 (R) | % change year on year | % change month on month |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 410 g beans | 12,60 | 15,14 | 20,2 | 0,5 |
| 250 g instant coffee | 45,56 | 48,47 | 6,4 | −1,0 |
| Eggs 1,5 dozen tray | 52,97 | 57,33 | 8,2 | 1,6 |
| 750 mℓ sunflower oil | 40,68 | 35,52 | −12,7 | −2,3 |
| Oranges per kg | 22,07 | 20,10 | −8,9 | −14,5 |
| Chicken giblets per kg | 37,73 | 46,75 | 23,9 | 2,2 |
| Chicken portions per 2 kg | 86,80 | 93,06 | 7,2 | 0,6 |
| **TOTAL** | **A** | **R316,37** | | |

Identify the food items that showed a decrease in both the month-on-month and year-on-year percentage change.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 & 2: **750 mℓ sunflower oil** (2RT first correct product)
Mark 3: **Oranges per kg** (1RT second correct product)

Teaching point: A decrease shows up as a NEGATIVE percentage. Sunflower oil is −12,7% (year on year) AND −2,3% (month on month); oranges are −8,9% AND −14,5%. Instant coffee is only negative in one column (−1,0% month on month, but +6,4% year on year), so it does not qualify.

subQuestions.questionText:
TABLE 1 shows the average comparative food prices for May 2022 and May 2023. Value **A** is the total of the May 2022 prices.

**TABLE 1: COMPARATIVE FOOD PRICES FOR SOME LUNCH ITEMS**

| Food items | Price May 2022 (R) | Price May 2023 (R) |
|---|---|---|
| 410 g beans | 12,60 | 15,14 |
| 250 g instant coffee | 45,56 | 48,47 |
| Eggs 1,5 dozen tray | 52,97 | 57,33 |
| 750 mℓ sunflower oil | 40,68 | 35,52 |
| Oranges per kg | 22,07 | 20,10 |
| Chicken giblets per kg | 37,73 | 46,75 |
| Chicken portions per 2 kg | 86,80 | 93,06 |
| **TOTAL** | **A** | **R316,37** |

Determine the missing value, **A**.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Value of A $= \text{R}12{,}60 + \text{R}45{,}56 + \text{R}52{,}97 + \text{R}40{,}68 + \text{R}22{,}07 + \text{R}37{,}73 + \text{R}86{,}80$ (1MA adding ALL correct values)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}298{,}41$ (1A simplification; NPU — no penalty for omitting the rand sign)

Teaching point: All SEVEN items in the May 2022 column must be added. Leaving one out loses the method mark, because the mark is for adding ALL the correct values.

subQuestions.questionText:
TABLE 1 shows that a tray of eggs containing 1,5 dozen eggs cost R52,97 during May 2022 (and R57,33 during May 2023).

Calculate the price of a dozen eggs during May 2022.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Price per dozen $= \text{R}52{,}97 \div 1{,}5$ (or $\times \dfrac{1}{1{,}5}$) (1A dividing by 1,5)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}35{,}31$ (1A simplification)

OR

Mark 1: 1 egg $= \dfrac{\text{R}52{,}97}{18}$ (1A dividing by 18)
Price per dozen $= \text{R}2{,}94277 \times 12$
Mark 2: $= \text{R}35{,}31$ (1A simplification)

OR

Mark 1: Price for ½ dozen $= \dfrac{\text{R}52{,}97}{3} = \text{R}17{,}65666$ (1A dividing by 3)
Price for a dozen $= \text{R}17{,}65666 \times 2$
Mark 2: $= \text{R}35{,}31$ (1A simplification; NPR)

Teaching point: 1,5 dozen means 18 eggs. Whether you divide the R52,97 by 1,5 or work out the price of one egg and multiply by 12, the answer is the same.

subQuestions.questionText:
TABLE 1 shows that oranges cost R22,07 per kg in May 2022 and R20,10 per kg in May 2023.

Write down the unit ratio, in the form **1 : …**, for the price of the oranges in May 2022 to the price of the oranges in May 2023.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 & 2: $= 22{,}07 : 20{,}10$ (1RT correct value + 1RT correct value)
$= 1 : 0{,}9107385591$
Mark 3: $\approx 1 : 0{,}91$ (1A simplification in the correct order; NPR)

Teaching point: A "unit ratio in the form 1 : …" means you must divide BOTH sides by the first number: $22{,}07 \div 22{,}07 = 1$ and $20{,}10 \div 22{,}07 = 0{,}91$. Keep the order the question gives — 2022 first, then 2023.

subQuestions.questionText:
TABLE 2 below gives definitions of terminology used in Mathematical Literacy.

**TABLE 2: TERMINOLOGY USED IN MATHEMATICAL LITERACY**

| Letter | Definition |
|---|---|
| A | An increase in the price of a basket of goods or services over time that is representative of the economy as a whole |
| B | Sum of all the values divided by the number of values |
| C | The income received from the item sold and the cost price of the item is the same |
| D | Value or values appearing most often in a data set |
| E | The difference between the highest and lowest values in a data set |
| F | An amount paid regularly at a particular rate for the use/loan of money |
| G | These are amounts that must be paid every month and which stay the same, like rent, school fees and transport costs |
| H | Middle value in an ordered data set |
| I | Expenses that change over time or from one week/month to the next, e.g. telephone and electricity costs |
| J | The point where the income exceeds the expenses |

Match the definition with the terminology below. Write only the letter (A–J).

**Break-even point**
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: **C** (2A correct letter)

The break-even point is where the income received from the item sold and the cost price of the item are the SAME — there is no profit and no loss.

Teaching point: Do not choose J. J describes the point where income EXCEEDS expenses, which is a profit, not break-even. At break-even the two amounts are exactly equal.

questions.title: Prepaid electricity till slip, home solar system payment options and income tax

subQuestions.questionText:
Miecke purchased prepaid electricity and received the following till slip. Note that some information has been omitted.

```
TAX INVOICE VAT NO. 4420106777
*** PREPAID ELECTRICITY ***
Electricity Municipal Prepaid
VAT REGISTRATION NO. 4370102313
Meter: 07032985769

DOMESTIC HOUSEHOLD TARIFF

Transaction Sequence No.: 56332515

Amount            R1 300,00
Units             *** kWh

Electricity       R1 130,43
VAT 15%           B
TOTAL             R1 300,00
```

Write down the meter number.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 & 2: **07032985769** (2RT correct number)

Teaching point: Read carefully — the slip also shows a VAT number (4420106777), a VAT registration number (4370102313) and a transaction sequence number (56332515). Only the number printed next to the word "Meter" is the meter number.

subQuestions.questionText:
Miecke purchased prepaid electricity and received the following till slip. Note that some information has been omitted.

```
TAX INVOICE VAT NO. 4420106777
*** PREPAID ELECTRICITY ***
Electricity Municipal Prepaid
VAT REGISTRATION NO. 4370102313
Meter: 07032985769

DOMESTIC HOUSEHOLD TARIFF

Transaction Sequence No.: 56332515

Amount            R1 300,00
Units             *** kWh

Electricity       R1 130,43
VAT 15%           B
TOTAL             R1 300,00
```

Determine the missing value, **B**.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: R1 300,00 and R1 130,43 read from the slip (1RT correct value)
Mark 2: $B = \text{R}1\,300{,}00 - \text{R}1\,130{,}43$ (1MA subtracting values)
Mark 3: $= \text{R}169{,}57$ (1A simplification)

OR

Mark 1: R1 130,43 read from the slip (1RT correct value)
Mark 2: $B = \text{R}1\,130{,}43 \times \dfrac{15}{100}$ (or $\times 0{,}15$) (1MA calculating 15%)
Mark 3: $= \text{R}169{,}56$ (1A simplification)

OR

Mark 1: R1 300 read from the slip (1RT correct value)
Mark 2: $B = \text{R}1\,300 \times \dfrac{15}{115}$ (1MA calculating $\tfrac{15}{115}$)
Mark 3: $= \text{R}169{,}57$ (1A simplification; AO — answer only gets full marks)

Teaching point: The TOTAL of R1 300,00 already includes VAT, so the VAT amount is the difference between the total and the amount excluding VAT. If you start from the VAT-inclusive total you must use $\tfrac{15}{115}$, not $\tfrac{15}{100}$.

subQuestions.questionText:
Miecke's prepaid electricity till slip shows:

```
Amount            R1 300,00
Units             *** kWh

Electricity       R1 130,43
VAT 15%           R169,57
TOTAL             R1 300,00
```

A partial residential electricity tariff table (excluding VAT) is shown below.

**TABLE 3: RESIDENTIAL ELECTRICITY TARIFF**

| Block | Consumption (kWh) | Tariff (R/kWh) |
|---|---|---|
| Block 1 | 0–350 | 2,19 |
| Block 2 | More than 350 | 2,91 |

Determine the number of kWh units Miecke purchased.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Amount for Block 1 $= 350 \text{ kWh} \times \text{R}2{,}19$ (1MA multiplying with the tariff)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}766{,}50$ (1CA simplification)
Mark 3: Amount left for Block 2 $= \text{R}1\,130{,}43 - \text{R}766{,}50 = \text{R}363{,}93$ (1MCA calculating the remaining amount in Block 2)
Mark 4: Units in Block 2 $= \dfrac{\text{R}363{,}93}{\text{R}2{,}91}$ (1MCA dividing by the tariff)
Mark 5: $= 125{,}0618557 \text{ kWh}$ (1CA simplification)
Mark 6: Total kWh received $= 350 \text{ kWh} + 125{,}0618557 \text{ kWh}$ (1MCA adding values)
Mark 7: $= 475{,}06 \text{ kWh}$ (1CA simplification)

OR (working with VAT-inclusive tariffs and the full R1 300)

Mark 1: Tariff (VAT included) $= \text{R}2{,}19 \times \dfrac{115}{100} = \text{R}2{,}5185$ and $\text{R}2{,}91 \times \dfrac{115}{100} = \text{R}3{,}3465$ (1A VAT calculation)
Mark 2: Amount spent in Block 1 $= 350 \text{ kWh} \times \text{R}2{,}5185 = \text{R}881{,}475$ (1MCA calculating the amount in Block 1)
Mark 3: Amount available for Block 2 $= \text{R}1\,300 - \text{R}881{,}475 = \text{R}418{,}525$ (1MCA calculating the remaining amount in Block 2)
Mark 4: Units in Block 2 $= \dfrac{\text{R}418{,}525}{\text{R}3{,}3465}$ (1MCA dividing by R3,3465)
Mark 5: $= 125{,}06 \text{ kWh}$ (1CA simplification)
Mark 6: Total kWh received $= 350 \text{ kWh} + 125{,}06 \text{ kWh}$ (1MCA adding values)
Mark 7: $= 475{,}06 \text{ kWh}$ (1CA simplification; NPR)

Teaching point: TABLE 3 gives tariffs EXCLUDING VAT, so match them with the electricity amount excluding VAT (R1 130,43). The first 350 units are always charged at the cheaper Block 1 rate; only the money that is left over buys units at the more expensive Block 2 rate.

subQuestions.questionText:
Miecke plans to install a home solar system unit consisting of solar panels, a battery and an inverter. She sees the advertisement below in a community newspaper showing the two different payment options for the same unit. **HOME SOLAR SYSTEM UNIT PAYMENT OPTIONS** | OPTION 1: RENT-TO-OWN | OPTION 2: CASH PRICE | |---|---| | Pay for 7 years at R1 549 p/m
Additional costs:
R782 initiation fee
Buy-out after rental period R7 820 | R78 200 (incl. VAT) | Write down the monthly instalment for the rent-to-own option.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 & 2: **R1 549** (2RT correct amount; NPU — no penalty for omitting the rand sign)

Teaching point: "p/m" means per month, so R1 549 p/m is the monthly instalment. The R782 initiation fee and the R7 820 buy-out are once-off amounts, not monthly instalments.

subQuestions.questionText:
The cash price of a home solar system unit is R78 200 (including 15% VAT).

Calculate, excluding VAT, the cash price of the home solar system unit.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: R78 200 read from the advertisement (1RT for R78 200)
Mark 2: Price excluding VAT $= \dfrac{\text{R}78\,200}{1{,}15}$ (1MA dividing by 1,15)
Mark 3: $= \text{R}68\,000$ (1A simplification)

OR

Mark 1: R78 200 (1RT)
Mark 2: Price excluding VAT $= \text{R}78\,200 \times \dfrac{100}{115}$ (1MA multiplying by $\tfrac{100}{115}$)
Mark 3: $= \text{R}68\,000$ (1A simplification)

OR

Mark 1: R78 200 (1RT)
Mark 2: VAT amount $= \text{R}78\,200 \times \dfrac{15}{115}$ (1MA multiplying by $\tfrac{15}{115}$)
$= \text{R}10\,199{,}999 \approx \text{R}10\,200$
Mark 3: Price excluding VAT $= \text{R}78\,200 - \text{R}10\,200 = \text{R}68\,000$ (1A simplification)

Teaching point: Going from a VAT-INCLUSIVE price back to the price excluding VAT means dividing by 1,15 (or multiplying by $\tfrac{100}{115}$). A common error is subtracting 15% of R78 200, which gives the wrong answer.

subQuestions.questionText:
The two payment options for the same home solar system unit are: | OPTION 1: RENT-TO-OWN | OPTION 2: CASH PRICE | |---|---| | Pay for 7 years at R1 549 p/m
Additional costs:
R782 initiation fee
Buy-out after rental period R7 820 | R78 200 (incl. VAT) | After seven years, Miecke decides to buy-out the rent-to-own option. Calculate the extra amount she has to pay compared to buying the home solar system unit for cash.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Number of months $= 12 \times 7 = 84 \text{ months}$ (1A correct number of months)
Rent-to-own total $= (\text{R}1\,549 \times 84) + \text{R}782 + \text{R}7\,820$
Mark 2: $= \text{R}130\,116 + \text{R}782 + \text{R}7\,820$ (1MCA adding ALL correct values)
Mark 3: $= \text{R}138\,718$ (1CA simplification)
Mark 4: Difference $= \text{R}138\,718 - \text{R}78\,200$ (1MCA subtracting values)
Mark 5: $= \text{R}60\,518$ (1CA simplification)

Teaching point: "Extra amount" means the difference between the two options. Remember that a rent-to-own agreement adds the once-off initiation fee AND the buy-out amount on top of the 84 monthly instalments — that is why it costs so much more than paying cash.

subQuestions.questionText:
Miecke is 45 years old and earns a monthly taxable income of R39 275,85 in the 2023/2024 tax year. She does not belong to a medical aid.

ANNEXURE A shows the annual tax table for individuals for the 2023/2024 tax year:

**TAX RATES FROM 1 MARCH 2023 TO 29 FEBRUARY 2024**

| Tax bracket | Taxable income (R) | Tax rates (R) |
|---|---|---|
| A | 1–237 100 | 18% of taxable income |
| B | 237 101–370 500 | 42 678 + 26% of taxable income above 237 100 |
| C | 370 501–512 800 | 77 362 + 31% of taxable income above 370 500 |
| D | 512 801–673 000 | 121 475 + 36% of taxable income above 512 800 |
| E | 673 001–857 900 | 179 147 + 39% of taxable income above 673 000 |
| F | 857 901–1 817 000 | 251 258 + 41% of taxable income above 857 900 |
| G | 1 817 001 and above | 644 489 + 45% of taxable income above 1 817 000 |

Identify the tax bracket that Miecke will use to calculate her income tax payable.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Annual taxable income $= \text{R}39\,275{,}85 \times 12$ (1MA multiplying by 12)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}471\,310{,}20$ (1A simplification)
Mark 3: **Tax Bracket C** (1MCA tax bracket C; AO — answer only gets full marks)

Teaching point: The tax table is an ANNUAL table, so a monthly income must first be multiplied by 12. R471 310,20 falls between R370 501 and R512 800, which is bracket C.

subQuestions.questionText:
Miecke is 45 years old and earns a monthly taxable income of R39 275,85 in the 2023/2024 tax year (an annual taxable income of R471 310,20). She does not belong to a medical aid.

**TAX RATES FROM 1 MARCH 2023 TO 29 FEBRUARY 2024**

| Tax bracket | Taxable income (R) | Tax rates (R) |
|---|---|---|
| A | 1–237 100 | 18% of taxable income |
| B | 237 101–370 500 | 42 678 + 26% of taxable income above 237 100 |
| C | 370 501–512 800 | 77 362 + 31% of taxable income above 370 500 |
| D | 512 801–673 000 | 121 475 + 36% of taxable income above 512 800 |
| E | 673 001–857 900 | 179 147 + 39% of taxable income above 673 000 |
| F | 857 901–1 817 000 | 251 258 + 41% of taxable income above 857 900 |
| G | 1 817 001 and above | 644 489 + 45% of taxable income above 1 817 000 |

**TAX REBATES 2023/2024**

| Rebate | Amount |
|---|---|
| Primary | R17 235 |
| Secondary (person 65 and older) | R9 444 |
| Tertiary (person 75 and older) | R3 145 |

**TAX THRESHOLDS 2023/2024**

| Age | Threshold |
|---|---|
| Under 65 | R95 750 |
| 65 and older | R148 217 |
| 75 and older | R165 689 |

Calculate Miecke's annual tax payable for the 2023/2024 tax year.
subQuestions.memoText:
Tax before rebate (bracket C: $77\,362 + 31\%$ of taxable income above $370\,500$)
Mark 1: $= \text{R}77\,362 + 31\%(\text{R}471\,310{,}20 - \text{R}370\,500)$ (1SF correct substitution)
$= \text{R}77\,362 + 31\%(\text{R}100\,810{,}20)$
Mark 2: $= \text{R}77\,362 + \text{R}31\,251{,}162$ (1MCA adding values)
Mark 3: $= \text{R}108\,613{,}162$ (1CA simplification)
Mark 4: Annual tax payable $= \text{R}108\,613{,}162 - \text{R}17\,235$ (1RT rebate: R17 235)
Mark 5: $= \text{R}91\,378{,}162 = \text{R}91\,378{,}16$ (1CA simplification)

OR (in one line)

Annual tax payable $= \text{R}77\,362 + 0{,}31(\text{R}471\,310{,}20 - \text{R}370\,500) - \text{R}17\,235$ (1SF correct substitution + 2MCA adding values + 1RT rebate R17 235)
$= \text{R}91\,378{,}16$ (1CA simplification)

Teaching point: The 31% is charged ONLY on the income above R370 500, not on the whole R471 310,20. Miecke is 45, so she qualifies for the PRIMARY rebate (R17 235) only — the secondary and tertiary rebates are for people 65 and older.

questions.title: Shoprite and Pick n Pay store and employee trends, and customer shopping times

subQuestions.questionText:
ANNEXURE B shows two graphs. GRAPH 2 shows the trends in the total number of employees at Shoprite and Pick n Pay stores for the period 2005 to 2023. Only 2005, 2014 and 2023 are labelled on the horizontal axis, and the vertical axis is marked at 50 000, 100 000 and 150 000 employees. The Pick n Pay line is dotted from 2005 to 2014 and solid from 2014 to 2023.

The approximate readings for the total number of Pick n Pay employees are:

| Year | Pick n Pay employees (approx.) |
|---|---|
| 2005 | 60 000 |
| 2006–2013 | rising steadily from about 62 000 to about 71 000 |
| 2014 | 72 000 |
| 2015 | 69 000 |
| 2016 | 69 000 |
| 2017 | 76 000 |
| 2018 | 83 000 |
| 2019 | 89 000 |
| 2020–2022 | about 90 000 |
| 2023 | 90 000 |

Identify the year in which there was a decrease in the number of employees in the Pick n Pay stores for the first time.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 & 2: **2015** (2RT correct year)

Teaching point: From 2005 up to 2014 the Pick n Pay line only climbs. The very first time the line turns downwards is between 2014 and 2015, so 2015 is the first year showing a decrease. After the dip the line climbs again to 90 000 in 2023.
subQuestions.topic: Data handling – Reading a line graph

subQuestions.questionText:
GRAPH 1 in ANNEXURE B shows the trends in the total number of Shoprite and Pick n Pay stores for the period 2014 to 2023. The endpoints printed on the graph are: Shoprite 1 581 stores in 2014 and 3 543 stores in 2023; Pick n Pay 1 128 stores in 2014 and **2 204 stores in 2023**.

It is projected that the number of Pick n Pay stores will increase by 95,39% from 2023 to 2032.

Determine, by means of calculations, the projected number of Pick n Pay stores in 2032.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: 2 204 read from the graph (1RT correct value 2 204)
Mark 2: Projected number of stores $= 2\,204 \times \dfrac{95{,}39}{100} + 2\,204$ (1MA percentage calculation)
$= 2\,102{,}3956 + 2\,204 = 4\,306{,}3956$
Mark 3: $= 4\,306 \text{ stores}$ (1CA simplification)

OR

Mark 1: 2 204 (1RT)
Mark 2: $= 2\,204 \times \dfrac{195{,}39}{100}$ (or $\times 1{,}9539$) (1MA percentage calculation)
Mark 3: $= 4\,306 \text{ stores}$ (1CA simplification; AO. Accept 4 307)

Teaching point: An INCREASE of 95,39% means the new value is 195,39% of the old value. You can either work out the increase and add it on, or multiply by 1,9539 in one step. A number of stores must be a whole number.

subQuestions.questionText:
ANNEXURE B shows two graphs about Shoprite and Pick n Pay.

GRAPH 1 (total number of STORES) shows for 2023: Shoprite **3 543** stores and Pick n Pay **2 204** stores.

GRAPH 2 (total number of EMPLOYEES) shows for 2023: Shoprite **153 726** employees and Pick n Pay **90 000** employees.

An analyst stated that Shoprite employed more employees per store than Pick n Pay during 2023.

Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether the analyst's statement is valid.
subQuestions.memoText:
Average Shoprite employees per store
Mark 1 & 2: $= 153\,726 \div 3\,543$ (1RT for 153 726; 1RT for 3 543)
Mark 3: $= 43{,}388653\ldots \text{ employees per store}$ (1CA simplification)

Average Pick n Pay employees per store
Mark 4: $= 90\,000 \div 2\,204$ (1RT both correct values)
Mark 5: $= 40{,}834845\ldots \text{ employees per store}$ (1CA simplification)

Mark 6: Since $43{,}39 > 40{,}83$, the statement is **VALID**. (1O conclusion; NPR)

Teaching point: "Per store" means divide the number of employees by the number of stores — and you must read the two values from TWO different graphs. A conclusion mark can only be awarded if at least a third of the calculation marks have been earned, so always show both averages before writing the conclusion.
subQuestions.topic: Data handling – Comparing two graphs / averages

subQuestions.questionText:
GRAPH 1 in ANNEXURE B shows the total number of Shoprite and Pick n Pay stores for each of the years 2014 to 2023 (10 years). The horizontal gridlines are drawn at 0, 1 000, 2 000, 3 000 and 4 000 stores. The approximate readings for the number of Shoprite stores are:

| Year | Shoprite stores (approx.) |
|---|---|
| 2014 | 1 581 (printed on the graph) |
| 2015 | 1 800 |
| 2016 | 1 880 |
| 2017 | 2 390 |
| 2018 | 2 450 |
| 2019 | 2 350 |
| 2020 | 2 380 |
| 2021 | 2 500 |
| 2022 | 3 020 |
| 2023 | 3 543 (printed on the graph) |

Determine, as a percentage, the probability of randomly selecting a year where the number of Shoprite stores is fewer than 2 000.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: numerator = 3 (the years 2014, 2015 and 2016 are the only years below the 2 000 gridline) (1RT correct numerator)
Mark 2: denominator = 10 (the graph covers 10 years, 2014 to 2023) (1RT correct denominator)
Probability $= \dfrac{3}{10} \times 100\%$
Mark 3: $= 30\%$ (1CA simplification; AO)

Teaching point: Count how many years the Shoprite line lies BELOW the 2 000 gridline, then divide by the total number of years shown. Multiply by 100 because the answer must be a percentage.

subQuestions.questionText:
A study relating to the amount of time spent (in minutes) by a selected number of customers in a store was conducted on a particular Saturday. On that Saturday, a total of 12 342 customers visited the store.

The times recorded (in minutes) were:

| | | | | | | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | 15 | 25 | 25 | 40 | 28 | 18 | 23 |
| 43 | 15 | 22 | 19 | 15 | 8 | 37 | 9 |
| 24 | 23 | 15 | 67 | 25 | 29 | 6 | 17 |
| 15 | 43 | 23 | 27 | 33 | 26 | 127 | 10 |

Write down the number of customers that represent the sample size and the number of customers that represent the population size for this study.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 & 2: Sample $= 32$ (1A counting to 32; 1A sample)
Mark 3: Population $= 12\,342$ (1A correct population)

OR

32 and 12 342 (2A sample in the correct order; 1A population in the correct order — no words needed)

Teaching point: The SAMPLE is the group actually measured (count the values in the data set — there are 4 rows of 8, so 32). The POPULATION is the whole group the sample was taken from — all 12 342 customers who visited the store that Saturday.

subQuestions.questionText:
A study was done on the amount of time (in minutes) that customers spent in a store on a particular Saturday.

Choose the correct option (**A**, **B**, **C**, **D** or **E**) that represents the stage in the data handling process that uses the measures of central tendency and spread.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: **E** — Analysing data (2A correct option)

Teaching point: The data handling cycle runs: pose a question → collect data → classify and organise → summarise → represent → analyse and interpret. Working out the mean, median, mode, range and interquartile range in order to draw conclusions is the ANALYSING stage.
subQuestions.topic: Data handling – The data handling cycle

subQuestions.questionText:
The times (in minutes) that 32 customers spent in a store were, in rank order:

6; 8; 9; 10; 12; 15; 15; 15; 15; 15; 17; 18; 19; 22; 23; 23; 23; 24; 25; 25; 25; 26; 27; 28; 29; 33; 37; 40; 43; 43; 67; 127

Give a reason why the value of 127 is considered to be an outlier in the data set.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 & 2: The value 127 is 60 minutes more than the second-highest time in the data set (127 − 67 = 60), so it lies far away from the rest of the data. (2O conclusion)

Teaching point: An outlier is a value that is very much larger or very much smaller than the rest of the data. Here almost all the times are under 45 minutes, so 127 minutes stands right out. Outliers pull the MEAN up, which is why the median is often a better average when outliers are present.

subQuestions.label: 3.2.4 (a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Shown below, in rank order, is selected data of the time (in minutes) spent by customers in the store:

6; 8; 9; 10; 12; 15; 15; 15; 15; 15; 17; 18; 19; 22; 23; 23; 24; 25; 25; 25; 26; 27; 28; 29; 33; 37; 40; 43; 43; 67; 127

An incomplete box-and-whisker plot of the same data has the following five-number summary:

| Value | Reading |
|---|---|
| Minimum | 6 |
| Lower quartile (Q1) | 15 |
| Median (Q2) | not shown |
| Upper quartile (Q3) | **Q3 — to be calculated** |
| Maximum | 127 |

Calculate the value of the upper quartile (Q3).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: The two middle values of the upper half are 28 and 29 (1RT correct values)
Mark 2: Quartile 3 $= \dfrac{28 + 29}{2}$ (1MA concept of quartile)
Mark 3: $= 28{,}5$ (1CA simplification; AO)

Teaching point: Q3 is the middle value of the upper half of the ordered data. When the upper half has an even number of values, Q3 is the average of the two middle values — here 28 and 29, giving 28,5.

subQuestions.label: 3.2.4 (b)
subQuestions.questionText:
Shown below, in rank order, is selected data of the time (in minutes) spent by customers in the store:

6; 8; 9; 10; 12; 15; 15; 15; 15; 15; 17; 18; 19; 22; 23; 23; 24; 25; 25; 25; 26; 27; 28; 29; 33; 37; 40; 43; 43; 67; 127

For the full data set the lower quartile (Q1) is 15 and the upper quartile (Q3) is 28,5. The value 127 is an outlier.

Vuyo stated that if the outlier value was removed from the data set, the new interquartile range (IQR) value would be 13.

Verify Vuyo's statement, showing ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: New Quartile 1 $= 15$ (1RT correct value)
Mark 2: New Quartile 3 $= 28$ (1RT correct value)
Mark 3: $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$ (1A correct formula)
Mark 4: $\text{IQR} = 28 - 15$ (1MCA subtracting values)
$= 13$
Mark 5: Vuyo is **CORRECT**. (1O conclusion)

Teaching point: Removing the outlier 127 leaves 30 values instead of 31, which shifts the quartile positions. The new Q3 becomes 28 (instead of 28,5) while Q1 stays at 15, so the IQR is exactly 13 — Vuyo's claim holds. Always state the formula IQR = Q3 − Q1 to earn that mark.

questions.title: 21st birthday party budget, DJ hire costs and function venue guest numbers

subQuestions.label: 4.1.1 (a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Lee's parents plan to celebrate his 21st birthday. This special event will be held at a popular hotel, starting at 18:00.

**TABLE 4: BUDGETED EXPENSES FOR THE PARTY**

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Cost of the venue | R750 deposit and R6 185 for the day |
| Food and drinks | R18 000 |
| Birthday cake | R1 250 |
| **OPTIONS FOR DISC JOCKEYS (DJs)** | |
| DJ Rain | R4 000 for 5 hours or less. Thereafter the tariff is an additional R1 250 per hour. |
| DJ 5-Star | R1 000 per hour or part thereof |
| DJ Cool | R6 000 for the party |

Write a formula to calculate the cost to hire DJ Rain for more than 5 hours in the following form:

**Cost = …**
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Cost $= \text{R}4\,000 + \ldots$ (1A fixed cost R4 000)
Mark 2: $\ldots + \text{R}1\,250 \times \ldots$ (1A multiplying hours with the tariff R1 250)
Mark 3: $\ldots \times (\text{number of hours exceeding }5)$ (1A number of hours more than 5)

So: **Cost = R4 000 + R1 250 × (number of hours exceeding 5)**

OR

Cost $= \text{R}4\,000 + \text{R}1\,250 \times n$, where $n$ = number of hours exceeding 5 (1A + 1A + 1A for defining $n$)

Teaching point: The R4 000 is a fixed amount that covers the first 5 hours. The extra R1 250 is only charged for each hour BEYOND 5 hours, so the variable part must be multiplied by (hours − 5), not by the total hours.
subQuestions.topic: Patterns and relationships – Writing a formula

subQuestions.label: 4.1.1 (b)
subQuestions.questionText:
DJ Rain charges R4 000 for 5 hours or less. Thereafter the tariff is an additional R1 250 per hour.

The table below represents the cost to hire DJ Rain.

**TABLE 5: COST TO HIRE DJ RAIN PER HOUR**

| Number of hours | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cost (in R) | 4 000 | 4 000 | **P** | 4 000 | 4 000 | **Q** | 6 500 | 7 750 | **R** |

Complete the table by calculating the missing values **P**, **Q** and **R**.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $P = \text{R}4\,000$ (1A value of P)
Mark 2 & 3: $Q = \text{R}4\,000 + \text{R}1\,250 \times 1 = \text{R}5\,250$ (2A value of Q)
Mark 4: $R = \text{R}4\,000 + \text{R}1\,250 \times 4 = \text{R}9\,000$ (1A value of R)

Teaching point: For 5 hours or less the cost stays flat at R4 000, so P (3 hours) = R4 000. From hour 6 onwards add R1 250 for every hour above 5: 6 hours → 1 extra hour, 9 hours → 4 extra hours. Check against the given values: 7 hours = 4 000 + 2 × 1 250 = 6 500 ✓ and 8 hours = 4 000 + 3 × 1 250 = 7 750 ✓.
subQuestions.topic: Patterns and relationships – Completing a table

subQuestions.label: 4.1.2 (a)
subQuestions.questionText:
DJ 5-Star charges R1 000 per hour or part thereof. The graph of DJ 5-Star's cost on the ANSWER SHEET is drawn as a series of horizontal line segments: it stays at R1 000 for any time up to and including 1 hour, then jumps to R2 000 for any time up to and including 2 hours, then to R3 000, and so on, up to R9 000 at 9 hours. Each horizontal segment starts with an open circle and ends with a closed circle.

Name the type of graph used to represent the cost to hire DJ 5-Star.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 & 2: **Step graph** (also accepted: stepwise graph) (2A correct name)

Teaching point: "Per hour or part thereof" always produces a step graph — the price stays the same right through a whole hour and then jumps suddenly to the next amount, so the graph looks like a flight of stairs instead of a smooth line.
subQuestions.topic: Patterns and relationships – Types of graphs

subQuestions.label: 4.1.2 (b)
subQuestions.questionText:
This is a graph-DRAWING task. On the ANSWER SHEET there is a grid titled 'COMPARISON OF THE COST FOR THE DIFFERENT DJs', with the number of hours playing (0 to 9) on the horizontal axis and the cost in rand (0 to R10 000) on the vertical axis. The step graph for DJ 5-Star and the horizontal line for DJ Cool (R6 000) are already drawn on the grid.

Use TABLE 5, showing the cost to hire DJ Rain for up to 9 hours, to draw a line graph on the same grid.

**TABLE 5: COST TO HIRE DJ RAIN PER HOUR**

| Number of hours | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cost (in R) | 4 000 | 4 000 | 4 000 | 4 000 | 4 000 | 5 250 | 6 500 | 7 750 | 9 000 |

Describe (or plot) the points you would use and the shape of the graph.
subQuestions.memoText:
CA from Question 4.1.1 (b).

Mark 1: starting point $(0 ; 4\,000)$ (1A)
Mark 2: the point $(5 ; 4\,000)$ (1A)
Mark 3: end point $(9 ; 9\,000)$ (1A)
Mark 4: joining ALL the points plotted on the slanted part of the graph (1A)

The graph therefore consists of TWO parts:
• a horizontal straight line from $(0 ; 4\,000)$ through $(1 ; 4\,000)$, $(2 ; 4\,000)$, $(3 ; 4\,000)$ and $(4 ; 4\,000)$ to $(5 ; 4\,000)$; and
• a straight slanted line joining $(5 ; 4\,000)$, $(6 ; 5\,250)$, $(7 ; 6\,500)$, $(8 ; 7\,750)$ and $(9 ; 9\,000)$.

Teaching point: The flat part shows the fixed R4 000 for the first 5 hours; the slanted part rises by exactly R1 250 for every extra hour, so those four points lie on a straight line. Use a ruler and label the line 'DJ Rain'.
subQuestions.topic: Patterns and relationships – Drawing a graph

subQuestions.questionText:
The budgeted expenses for Lee's 21st birthday party are:

**TABLE 4: BUDGETED EXPENSES FOR THE PARTY**

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Cost of the venue | R750 deposit and R6 185 for the day |
| Food and drinks | R18 000 |
| Birthday cake | R1 250 |
| **OPTIONS FOR DISC JOCKEYS (DJs)** | |
| DJ Rain | R4 000 for 5 hours or less. Thereafter the tariff is an additional R1 250 per hour. |
| DJ 5-Star | R1 000 per hour or part thereof |
| DJ Cool | R6 000 for the party |

Lee's parents decide to hire DJ 5-Star for the 21st birthday party. DJ 5-Star will provide the music entertainment from 18:00 until 01:30.

Determine the total budgeted expenses for the party.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Time $= 18{:}00 \text{ to } 01{:}30 = 7 \text{ hrs } 30 \text{ min} \approx 8 \text{ hrs}$ (1A calculating hours)
Mark 2: Cost for DJ $= 8 \times \text{R}1\,000$ (1MCA multiplying by R1 000)
Mark 3: $= \text{R}8\,000$ (1CA simplification)
Mark 4: Total cost $= \text{R}18\,000 + \text{R}750 + \text{R}6\,185 + \text{R}1\,250 + \text{R}8\,000$ (1MCA adding all values)
Mark 5: $= \text{R}34\,185$ (1CA simplification)

Teaching point: DJ 5-Star charges "per hour OR PART THEREOF", so the 7 hours 30 minutes must be rounded UP to a full 8 hours. Remember to include BOTH venue amounts — the R750 deposit and the R6 185 for the day.

subQuestions.questionText:
The three DJ options available for Lee's 21st birthday party were:

| DJ | Tariff |
|---|---|
| DJ Rain | R4 000 for 5 hours or less. Thereafter the tariff is an additional R1 250 per hour. |
| DJ 5-Star | R1 000 per hour or part thereof |
| DJ Cool | R6 000 for the party |

Lee's parents chose DJ 5-Star.

Give ONE reason why Lee's parents did not choose DJ Cool.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 & 2: Any ONE valid reason, for example — He charges a flat/fixed rate of R6 000 for the party, which is not economical if the party ends early (2O correct reason)

OR

He has a bad reputation.

Teaching point: DJ Cool charges R6 000 no matter how long he plays. Because DJ 5-Star only cost R8 000 for 8 hours (R1 000 per hour), a shorter party would be cheaper with a per-hour DJ — a flat rate only pays off if the party runs very long.

subQuestions.questionText:
The hotel has three other smaller venues, each accommodating a maximum number of guests per function, as listed below:

| Venue | Maximum guests |
|---|---|
| Cinema-style venue | 400 guests |
| Sit-down venue without dancing space | 250 guests |
| Sit-down venue with dancing space | 200 guests |

TABLE 6 shows the number of guests accommodated for functions at the three venues during a specific month in 2022 and 2023.

**TABLE 6: ACTUAL NUMBER OF GUESTS PER FUNCTION**

| Year | Number of guests |
|---|---|
| 2023 | 180; 350; 400; 200; 215; 90; 150; 230; 160 |
| 2022 | 360; 160; 300; 70; 160; 200; 240 |

Write, as a decimal, the probability that a cinema-style venue was chosen as a suitable function venue for all the functions held during 2022 and 2023.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: numerator $= 4$ (1A numerator)
Mark 2: denominator $= 16$ (1A denominator)
Probability $= \dfrac{4}{16}$
Mark 3: $= 0{,}25$ (1CA simplification)

Teaching point: The other two venues hold at most 250 guests, so ONLY the cinema-style venue (400 guests) can take a function with more than 250 guests. Those functions are 350 and 400 in 2023 and 360 and 300 in 2022 — that is 4 functions out of the 9 + 7 = 16 functions held over the two years.

subQuestions.questionText:
TABLE 6 shows the number of guests accommodated for functions at three hotel venues during a specific month in 2022 and 2023.

**TABLE 6: ACTUAL NUMBER OF GUESTS PER FUNCTION**

| Year | Number of guests |
|---|---|
| 2023 | 180; 350; 400; 200; 215; 90; 150; 230; 160 |
| 2022 | 360; 160; 300; 70; 160; 200; 240 |

Determine the median number of guests accommodated during 2023.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Arranged in ascending order: 90; 150; 160; 180; **200**; 215; 230; 350; 400 (1A arranging)
Mark 2 & 3: Median $= 200$ (2A median; AO)

Teaching point: The median is the MIDDLE value of the ordered data. There are 9 values in 2023, so the median is the 5th value. The most common mistake is finding the middle of the unordered list — always sort the data first.

subQuestions.questionText:
TABLE 6 shows the number of guests accommodated for functions at three hotel venues during a specific month in 2022 and 2023.

**TABLE 6: ACTUAL NUMBER OF GUESTS PER FUNCTION**

| Year | Number of guests |
|---|---|
| 2023 | 180; 350; 400; 200; 215; 90; 150; 230; 160 |
| 2022 | 360; 160; 300; 70; 160; 200; 240 |

The manager stated that the range of the number of guests per function during 2022 is the same as the range of the number of guests per function during 2023.

Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether his statement is valid.
subQuestions.memoText:
Range 2022
Mark 1: highest = 360 and lowest = 70 (1RT both correct values)
Mark 2: $= 360 - 70$ (1MCA concept of range)
Mark 3: $= 290$ (1CA simplification)

Range 2023
Mark 4: $= 400 - 90 = 310$ (1A range)

Mark 5: Since $290 \neq 310$, his statement is **NOT VALID**. (1O conclusion)

Teaching point: Range = highest value − lowest value. Work out the range for each year separately and then compare. A conclusion mark is only awarded if the supporting calculations are shown.

questions.title: Indian Union budget pie charts, currency conversions and house price inflation

subQuestions.questionText:
The pie charts on ANNEXURE C show the Indian Union budgets for income and expenditure for 2023/2024. Some values have been omitted.

Choose the correct word from those given in brackets. Write down only the word next to the question number (5.1.1).

A budget is a (deficit/surplus/balanced) budget when the income is less than the expenditure.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 & 2: **Deficit** (2A correct word)

Teaching point: Deficit = shortfall (income < expenditure); surplus = money left over (income > expenditure); balanced = income exactly equals expenditure.

subQuestions.questionText:
The pie chart on ANNEXURE C titled 'Indian Union Budget Income Sources in 2023-2024 (45,03 lakh crores)' shows the following income sources. The GST percentage has been omitted.

| Income source | Percentage of income |
|---|---|
| Borrowings | 34% |
| Corporation tax | 15% |
| Income tax | 15% |
| GST | … (missing) |
| Excise duties | 7% |
| Non-tax receipts | 6% |
| Customs | 4% |
| Non-debt capital receipts | 2% |

General sales tax (GST) is a tax that is similar to VAT in South Africa.

Calculate the missing percentage for GST on the pie chart.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: reading all the given percentages (1RT ALL correct values)
Mark 2: GST% $= 100\% - (15\% + 15\% + 4\% + 7\% + 6\% + 2\% + 34\%)$ (1MA adding and subtracting)
$= 100\% - 83\%$
Mark 3: $= 17\%$ (1CA simplification; AO)

Teaching point: All the slices of a pie chart must add up to 100%. Add every percentage that IS shown, then subtract the total from 100%.

subQuestions.questionText:
The pie chart on ANNEXURE C titled 'Indian Union Budget Income Sources in 2023-2024 (45,03 lakh crores)' shows the following income sources (GST = 17%):

| Income source | Percentage of income |
|---|---|
| Borrowings | 34% |
| GST | 17% |

| Excise duties | 7% |

CA from Question 5.1.2 for GST. Borrowings = 34%, so any THREE sources adding to 34% are accepted.

subQuestions.questionText:
The pie chart on ANNEXURE C titled 'Indian Union Budget 2023-2024 Expenditure (45,03 lakh crores)' shows that **interest payments make up 20%** of the expenditure.

The currency used in India is the rupee. India also has different denominations for the larger currency amounts.

NOTE: 100 000 rupees = 1 lakh; 100 lakhs = 1 crore

Sanji calculated, in lakh crores, the amount spent on interest payments. He rounded off his answer to the nearest whole number.

Sanji stated that the rounded answer he calculated did not make much difference in rupees when compared to the non-rounded answer.

Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether his statement is valid.
subQuestions.memoText:
Interest payments
Mark 1: $= 20\% \times 45{,}03 \text{ lakh crore}$ (1RT both correct values)
Mark 2: $= 9{,}006 \text{ lakh crore}$ (1A simplification)

Unrounded, in rupees
Mark 3: $= 9{,}006 \times 100 \times 100\,000 = 90\,060\,000 \text{ rupees}$ (1C conversion)

Rounded, in rupees
Mark 4: $= 9 \times 100 \times 100\,000 = 90\,000\,000 \text{ rupees}$ (1R rounded answer)

Mark 5: Difference $= 90\,060\,000 - 90\,000\,000 = 60\,000 \text{ rupees}$ (1CA difference)
Mark 6: His statement is **NOT VALID**. (1O conclusion)

OR

Interest payments $= 20\% \times 45{,}03 = 9{,}006 \text{ lakh crore}$ (1RT + 1A)
Difference $= 9{,}006 - 9{,}000 = 0{,}006 \text{ lakh crore}$ (1R rounded answer; 1CA difference)
Amount in rupees $= 0{,}006 \times 100 \times 100\,000 = 60\,000$ (1C conversion)
His statement is **NOT VALID**. (1O conclusion)

Teaching point: 1 lakh crore = 100 crore = 100 × 100 000 rupees, so a difference that looks tiny (0,006) becomes 60 000 rupees in real money. When you work with very large denominations, small rounding errors can still be worth a lot.

subQuestions.questionText:
In 2024, South Africa received R302,4 billion from corporate income tax.

NOTE: R1 000 000 = 4 447 989,1 rupees and 4 447 989,1 rupees = 44,479891 lakhs

Convert R302,4 billion to million rands.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Amount expressed in million $= \text{R}302{,}4 \text{ billion} \times 1\,000$ (1MA multiplying by 1 000)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}302\,400 \text{ million}$ (or R302 400 000 000) (1A simplification; AO)

Teaching point: 1 billion = 1 000 million, so multiply the number of billions by 1 000 to get millions.

subQuestions.questionText:
In 2024, South Africa received R302,4 billion (= R302 400 million) from corporate income tax.

NOTE: R1 000 000 = 4 447 989,1 rupees and 4 447 989,1 rupees = 44,479891 lakhs
Also: 100 000 rupees = 1 lakh and 100 lakhs = 1 crore

Hence, convert the South African corporate income tax to lakh crore.
subQuestions.memoText:
CA from Question 5.2.1.

Mark 1: $\text{R}302\,400 \text{ million} = \text{R}302\,400 \times 44{,}479891 \text{ lakh}$ (1MA multiplying by the correct exchange rate)
Mark 2: $= 13\,450\,719{,}04 \text{ lakh}$ (1CA simplification)
Mark 3: $= 13\,450\,719{,}04 \div 100$ (1MCA dividing by 100)
Mark 4: $= 134\,507{,}1904 \text{ lakh crore}$ (1CA simplification)

OR

Mark 1: $\text{R}302\,400\,000\,000 = \dfrac{\text{R}302\,400\,000\,000}{\text{R}1\,000\,000} \times 4\,447\,989{,}1$ (1MA multiplying by the correct exchange rate)
Mark 2: $= 1{,}345071904 \times 1\,000\,000\,000\,000$ (1CA simplification)
Mark 3: $\div 100\,000 \div 100$ (1MCA)
Mark 4: $= 134\,507{,}1904 \text{ lakh crore}$ (1CA simplification)

OR

Mark 1: $\text{R}1\,000\,000 = 0{,}44479891 \text{ lakh crore}$ (1C ÷ 10 000 000)
Mark 2: $\text{R}302\,400\,000\,000 = \dfrac{302\,400\,000\,000 \times 0{,}44479891}{1\,000\,000}$ (1MA multiplying by the correct exchange rate; 1MCA ÷ 1 000 000)
Mark 4: $= 134\,507{,}1904 \text{ lakh crore}$ (1CA simplification; NPR)

Teaching point: Work in steps — first change rand to rupees using the given rate, then change rupees to lakhs, then divide by 100 because 100 lakhs = 1 crore. Writing each conversion on its own line makes it much easier to check.

subQuestions.questionText:
A house in Chennai, India, is valued at 5 000 000 rupees at the end of 2024.

TABLE 7 shows the inflation rates in India for house prices for the last five years.

**TABLE 7: INFLATION RATES IN INDIA FOR THE LAST FIVE YEARS**

| Year | Inflation rate |
|---|---|
| 2024 | 8% |
| 2023 | 7,5% |
| 2022 | 7% |
| 2021 | 6,5% |
| 2020 | 6% |

Calculate how much the house was worth at the end of 2022.
subQuestions.memoText:
Price at the end of 2023
Mark 1: divide by 1,08 (or 108%) (1A identifying 1,08 or 108%)
Mark 2: $= 5\,000\,000 \div 1{,}08$ (1MA dividing by 1,08 or 108%)
Mark 3: $= 4\,629\,629{,}63 \text{ rupees}$ (1CA simplification)

Price at the end of 2022
Mark 4: divide by 1,075 (or 107,5%) (1MCA identifying 1,075 or 107,5%)
Mark 5: $= 4\,629\,629{,}63 \div 1{,}075$ (1MA dividing by 1,075 or 107,5%)
Mark 6: $= 4\,306\,632{,}214 \text{ rupees}$ (1CA simplification)

OR

Price at end of 2023 $= 5\,000\,000 \times \dfrac{100}{108} = 4\,629\,629{,}63$ rupees (1A + 1MA + 1CA)
Price at end of 2022 $= 4\,629\,629{,}63 \times \dfrac{100}{107{,}5} = 4\,306\,632{,}214$ rupees (1MCA + 1MA + 1CA)

OR (in one line)

Price at end of 2022 $= 5\,000\,000 \times \dfrac{100}{108} \times \dfrac{100}{107{,}5} = 4\,306\,632{,}214 \text{ rupees}$ (1A identifying 1,08 or 108%; 1MA multiplying by $\tfrac{100}{108}$; 1MCA identifying 1,075 or 107,5%; 1MA multiplying by $\tfrac{100}{107{,}5}$; 2CA simplification; NPU; NPR)

Teaching point: You are working BACKWARDS in time, so you DIVIDE by the inflation factor instead of multiplying. Use the 2024 rate (8%) to step back from 2024 to 2023, then the 2023 rate (7,5%) to step back from 2023 to 2022 — each year uses its own rate.
